title: Quarter Tone Waltz
identity: Gordan Tudor, Quarter Tone Waltz (2010), for solo alto saxophone, Donemus D16436. Donemus’s public single-page score excerpt contains later bars (60–86) rather than the full work. A Josip Nochta Saxophone Competition program lists it in first-round repertoire.

evidence.claim: Donemus public notation excerpt identifies the piece and publisher number and shows bars 60–86 with quarter-tone fingerings and technique instructions.
Josip Nochta competition program lists Quarter Tone Waltz in first-round repertoire.
Croatian Ministry of Culture listing identifies the work among selected compositions in a public composition-support program; it does not describe saxophone demands.

score_observations.observation: The single-page excerpt covers bars 60–86. It shows repeated slap-tongue entries, extensive quarter-tone fingering indications, dense scalar runs with quintuplets and other rapid subdivisions, a section marked quasi an octave higher using third-octave fingering without the octave key, and a high-register closing line. Only this excerpt is available; full range and distribution of effects are unknown.

review_focus: Inference from the visible late excerpt: verify quarter-tone fingerings and third-octave response, then assess whether the long rapid passage and repeated slap attacks fit the intended performer. Competition listing establishes repertoire context, not a difficulty level.
collection_flag: Original unaccompanied alto saxophone work with a verified competition first-round listing; full score remains unavailable in the preview.

listening.description: Video listing identifies Dimitrii Uvarov performing the work at the Josip Nochta Competition.
listening.verification: Search result confirms title/performer; playback not auditioned.

score_links.description: Donemus one-page notation excerpt covering bars 60–86; visually inspected.

gaps: Only a late single-page excerpt is public; full score, opening, written range, and full work demands remain unknown.
The competition program was checked as repertoire evidence; no performance audio was auditioned.
